themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can make them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On ad supply integrity the models say the open web is financially hooked on fake volume and that verification costs more than faking does; on agentic traffic they would bribe agents into declaring themselves with faster lanes and better prices; on journey orchestration and the semantic context layer they call the blocker siloed bonuses and departmental politics rather than any missing technology.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable rank or denominator because answers are personalized and drift week to week; identity resolution has no way to know who is really the same person without recruiting consenting people as a truth set; incrementality faces platforms that adapt to the holdout; and the ad supply answers note that outcome signals are themselves sparse, laggy and spoofable.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say black-box ad platforms and already-trained models cannot show person-level proof, leaving canary identities and expiring audiences as the ceiling; the ad supply answers make the same move by judging spend against outcomes seen in your own data instead of vendor-reported impressions.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three would build an approved-claim library and constrain what the model may say, because deciding whether wording crosses a line is a contextual legal judgment; on the semantic context layer they argue a single definition of customer is the wrong target and that conflicting meanings must be disclosed rather than merged.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution every model puts a proxy or gateway in front of martech writes with spend, rate and audience caps because vendors offer no rollback; the consent answers put a single checkpoint on every path data leaves the warehouse, and the orchestration answers route all sends through one shared contact log or kill switch.
